summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September, in line with the central bank's survey of economists and up from 1.7% in August, and yearly inflation is 33.4%. Prices are up 23.6% so far in 2026. Reserves were about $48.7 billion on Oct 5 and the central bank has been buying dollars. The IMF's third program review is still open after a Sep 21 to 29 mission. Argentine stocks move on inflation prints, reserves and the IMF, and energy names also ride Vaca Muerta shale output and oil prices.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

summary: Brazil voted on Oct 4 and the result surprised markets. Flavio Bolsonaro took about 47% of valid votes to Lula's about 45%, so the two meet in a runoff on Oct 25. Investors read his lead as a sign of spending cuts and reform, and Brazilian stocks and the real jumped: the Ibovespa rose 7.7% on Oct 5 and hit a new record of 209,067 on Oct 9, with the real near 5.00 per dollar. The central bank cut the Selic to 13.75% on Sep 16, but September inflation came in at 4.58% over 12 months, above the 4.5% ceiling, which limits more cuts. The rally has priced in a Bolsonaro win (prediction markets near 87% to 89% on Oct 10), so a Lula comeback on Oct 25 is the main risk, and a 25% US Section 301 tariff on many Brazilian goods (since Jul 22) still hangs over exporters and the Pix payment system. The runoff has tightened: Quaest (Oct 14) and Datafolha (Oct 15, per O Povo) both show 51% to 49% for Flavio Bolsonaro, inside the margin of error.
for_you: The Oct 25 runoff is close to a coin flip again. NU is now 'Buy zone now' (14.73, zone 14.02 to 15.10), but wait until after the vote before buying or selling puts on Brazil names: a Lula win could knock Brazilian banks 5% to 10% in a day. The BBD insider cluster (22 insiders, about $100 million, last buys Sep 28) still stands. MELI is rated Avoid.

summary: The US and China extended their October 2025 trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US and 31% on US goods into China, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. On Oct 9 China and the EU reached an interim understanding to roughly halve Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU over four years, and China will cut duties on about EUR 4 billion of EU goods; EU leaders still have to approve it. China is also pushing into memory chips: CXMT's fifth generation DRAM platform is in mass production and its world share passed 10%, which hit Micron and Korean chipmakers on Oct 12. Chinese large caps are weak, with the Shanghai 50 at a 14 month low. September exports rose 36.3% from a year ago and the monthly surplus hit $133.5 billion (Oct 14), with chip exports up 108.1%.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. AAPL is 'Accumulate on pullback', QCOM is 'Wait' and NVDA is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' on Oct 15 data. A record trade surplus raises the odds of a new tariff fight before the Jan 10 rare earth deadline, and rising Chinese chip exports back the CXMT worry for MU. Size swings normally and skip memory.

summary: Europe is fighting an energy shock from the Iran war. Euro area inflation was 3.2% in August, with energy up 14.3% from a year ago, and markets expect the ECB to keep raising rates from a deposit rate of about 2.50% (next decision Oct 29). The brief Russia Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' has failed: Zelenskyy said Ukraine will resume strikes on Russian refineries, and Russia reported a hit on the Ryazan refinery on Oct 15, which keeps diesel tight into winter. ASML beat and raised on Oct 14. High energy hurts chemicals and industry, while oil majors and banks gain.
for_you: Europe is fighting energy driven inflation, so more ECB hikes are likely. European banks (SAN, ING) benefit. ASML is the one European name that matters for your AI themes; watch it around its earnings.

summary: The US-Iran war that began Feb 28, 2026 has left the Strait of Hormuz mostly shut to commercial ships for over seven months. The war is now inside Saudi Arabia: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on Oct 10, and on Oct 14 a ballistic missile hit an Aramco office building at its Dhahran headquarters, damaging the floors used by top executives. Ships keep getting hit: UKMTO reported a tanker and two container ships struck near Hormuz on Oct 13. Brent was about $106.30 on the morning of Oct 14. A Houthi official said Russia and China have reached out about a ceasefire. Qatar shipped only 18 LNG cargoes in the war's first six months against 509 a year earlier. Most Gulf champions like Aramco are not US listed, so the US trade is through oil producers, US LNG exporters, oil service firms and the KSA ETF.
for_you: This is the biggest outside risk to your whole dashboard. Oil above $100 because of Hormuz feeds US inflation, Fed hikes and market swings. Helped: CVX and LNG exporters. If you hold swings, a big Gulf headline is the most likely reason for a sudden gap down, so always have stops set.

summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, and said a cut is off the table for now. Inflation is forecast at 5.2% this fiscal year, pushed up by oil above $100, which India mostly imports. On Oct 12 the rupee rebounded about 1% to near 95.7 to 95.8 per dollar after RBI steps to curb dollar demand in the spot market, but stocks fell for another day as bond yields rose for a fourth session and foreign outflows reached about Rs 3 lakh crore; the Sensex was near 71,900 midday. The February trade deal with the US has stalled, and a 10% US Section 301 tariff has applied to most Indian goods since Jul 24. A weak rupee helps IT exporters like Infosys; higher rates and oil weigh on banks and consumers. September consumer inflation rose to 5.54% (Oct 12), above the RBI's 5.2% forecast.
for_you: India just raised rates and the rupee is weak. That helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) and hurts banks and travel. Nothing here is on your lists; low priority.

summary: The Bank of Japan raised its rate to 1.25% in September, the highest since 1995, and another hike is possible at the Oct 30 meeting. The global AI selloff hit Tokyo hard on Oct 15: the Nikkei fell 4.9% to 64,425.95, its third biggest point drop ever, with Advantest down about 15% and SoftBank Group down 8% to 10%. The yen firmed to just under 158 per dollar as investors sought safety. A weak yen helps exporters like Toyota and Sony, and higher rates help the big banks. The Nikkei rebounded about 1.4% to 1.8% on Oct 16 as Wall Street steadied.
for_you: A weak yen helps Japanese exporters and higher rates help Japanese banks. These are not on your setup lists. The BOJ meets Oct 30; a surprise hike can jolt US tech for a day or two, so keep that date in mind for open swings.

summary: The peso fell to about 18.4 per dollar on Oct 9, its weakest since November 2025. The trigger was Banxico's Oct 8 minutes, which left the door open to rate cuts from 6.50% and said Mexico need not follow the Fed, so the carry trade that held the peso up is weakening. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican companies' profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US.
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korean stocks are in a bear market. The KOSPI fell 7.57% to 5,554.22 on Oct 15, its seventh straight loss and lowest close since April 7, tripping a sidecar and a Level 1 circuit breaker; Korea Times puts it about 40% below its June 19 peak of 9,385. SK hynix fell about 11% and Samsung about 9.5% on doubts about AI returns, a possible memory glut from China's CXMT, and the chance of another US rate hike. Server DRAM spot prices are still rising, so the stocks are falling faster than the business. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.0% in August and meets Oct 22; SK hynix reports Oct 28 and Samsung Oct 29. Samsung and SK hynix have no regular US listing, so US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, Korean bank ADRs and Coupang. On Oct 16 the index bounced: about 2.1% to 5,668.05 early (AP) and about 4.1% to 5,782.62 in a later Saxo update; the close was not confirmed at writing.
for_you: Korea is a memory chip market, and memory is breaking down. Skip MU and memory swings until the selling stops. Avoid new buys in Korean bank ADRs before the Oct 22 Bank of Korea decision.

summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. On Oct 15 TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2%, a 66.4% gross margin, a Q4 guide of $52.3 to $54.3 billion, and raised 2026 growth to about 44%, saying AI demand is far above supply. Its shares still fell about 2% and the Taiex had its sixth biggest point drop ever, with record net foreign selling of NT$302.56 billion, as global investors cut AI exposure on rate and debt fears. The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week.
for_you: Taiwan is the AI factory. TSMC sales are still growing over 50% a year, which supports NVDA, AMD and the whole AI compute theme. TSMC reports Thursday Oct 15: avoid opening new AI chip swings before that call, and use any post earnings dip in NVDA (Buy zone now) as a long term entry.
